I've ported the calculator to Zig in `src/main.zig`; `node check.mjs` builds it and passes all 6 example cases. `build.sh` compiles an optimized, stripped binary to `./app`.

Beyond the examples, I ran the original JavaScript and the Zig binary on the same inputs and compared their output byte for byte. They matched on 4 test files of about 40,000 lines each. These mixed the checker's own expression generator, random junk characters, and stress cases: parentheses nested 200,000 deep, 300,000 min
